description: We don't fear the void—we extract its data.
summary:
FLARE-X (Flame in Freefall) is an AI-powered research and decision-support platform designed to improve fire safety for future human space exploration. It brings together NASA combustion investigations, experimental data, accident records and fire-prevention research into a unified interactive dashboard.

The platform enables users to explore and compare combustion investigations, rank their relevance to different mission environments such as lunar habitats, Mars bases and space stations, and examine how combustion behaviour changes under different experimental conditions. Its AI-powered Mission Intelligence assistant retrieves relevant research evidence and generates mission-specific insights and safety recommendations. Additional capabilities include interactive flame visualisation, scientific data analysis, experimental validation checks and evidence-based research exploration.

FLARE-X addresses the challenge of making complex combustion research accessible and actionable. By connecting scientific findings with practical engineering considerations, it aims to help researchers identify knowledge gaps, support predictive fire-safety modelling and inform the development of safer spacecraft, habitats and future exploration systems.
details:
Project Functionality and Working Principle

FLARE-X (Flame in Freefall) is an AI-powered research and decision-support platform developed to make combustion science research more accessible and useful for future space missions. It integrates NASA combustion investigations, experimental conditions, accident records and fire-prevention research into a unified platform.

Users can explore and compare investigations, examine experimental findings and identify research relevant to specific mission environments, including lunar habitats, Martian bases, space stations and pressurised rovers. The Mission Intelligence module uses habitat-specific relevance scoring to rank investigations and identify the research most applicable to a selected mission environment.

The integrated AI research assistant retrieves relevant information from the available research database, answers scientific questions and connects its responses to supporting evidence. It helps users understand combustion phenomena, compare experimental findings and identify potential fire-safety considerations.

Scientific Analysis and Engineering Approach

The platform includes an interactive Flame Lab for exploring flame behaviour, scientific data analysis tools for examining experimental measurements, and validation checks for assessing data consistency and selected physical relationships. Users can upload CSV and Excel datasets to perform statistical analysis, identify trends and examine relationships between experimental variables.

The system also generates mission-specific safety recommendations by connecting available research findings with considerations such as atmospheric composition, combustible materials, fire detection and suppression.

Technologies and Development Tools

The frontend is developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript to provide an interactive research interface. The backend uses Python and FastAPI, with SQLite for structured data storage. Data processing and analysis use Python scientific libraries, including Pandas, NumPy and SciPy. The AI assistant uses evidence-retrieval techniques, with optional local language-model integration.

Innovation, Benefits and Intended Impact

FLARE-X brings scientific research exploration, mission-specific investigation ranking, AI-assisted knowledge retrieval and experimental data analysis together in one workflow. Rather than treating NASA research as isolated datasets, it connects experimental evidence to practical engineering questions.

Its intended impact is to support researchers and aerospace engineers in identifying knowledge gaps, improving the interpretation of combustion experiments and informing the development of safer spacecraft, lunar habitats and future human exploration systems. The platform is designed as a research and decision-support tool, not a certified fire-safety prediction system.
